title: File the annual unclaimed property holder report (Texas)
description: Businesses holding property that has gone unclaimed — uncashed payroll or vendor checks, customer credits and refunds, unused gift cards, deposits — must report and turn it over to the state each year, after sending the owner a due diligence notice before the deadline. The annual report and payment are due July 1 for general property. A negative report is required even when the business holds nothing. A civil penalty of up to $100 a day applies to a delinquent report or payment. Which state's law applies depends on the owner's last known address, or the business's state of incorporation when there is none, so a business can owe reports to several states.

feeDetail.note: There is no fee to file or register.

penalty.note: Civil penalty of up to $100 a day for a delinquent report or payment.

title: Notify residents and regulators of a data breach within 60 days (Texas)
description: If personal information of residents of the state is acquired without authorization, notify affected residents within 60 days of discovering the breach and the Attorney General within 30 days if 250 or more residents are affected (Tex. Bus. & Com. Code 521.053). This is an event-driven duty, so it has no calendar date. Sources in the PR describe the state's rule in different words; check the statute for the exact trigger and content of the notice.

feeDetail.note: There is no fee to file or register.

penalty.note: The attorney general may seek up to $100 for each individual owed notice for each consecutive day of failure, capped at $250,000 per breach, in addition to a $2,000 to $50,000 penalty per violation (Business and Commerce Code 521.151).
